# user commands

Every `user` command, with the arguments and options the console actually defines.

## `user:add`

Create a user who can sign in (email + password, bound to a tenant).

```bash
bin/semitexa user:add
```

| option | takes a value |
|---|---|
| `--email` | yes |
| `--password` | yes |
| `--tenant` | yes |
| `--name` | yes |
| `--role` | yes |

## `user:disable`

Disable a user account (--enable restores it).

```bash
bin/semitexa user:disable
```

| option | takes a value |
|---|---|
| `--email` | yes |
| `--tenant` | yes |
| `--enable` | no |

## `user:list`

List sign-in accounts, with their tenant, role and lock state.

```bash
bin/semitexa user:list
```

| option | takes a value |
|---|---|
| `--tenant` | yes |
| `--all` | no |

## `user:password`

Set a user password (also clears any lockout).

```bash
bin/semitexa user:password
```

| option | takes a value |
|---|---|
| `--email` | yes |
| `--tenant` | yes |
| `--password` | yes |
